title: STAGE BY STAGE THROUGH THE WILDERNESS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites left Rameses and camped at Sukkoth. They left Sukkoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the desert. They left Etham, turned back to Pi Hahiroth, to the east of Baal Zephon, and camped near Migdol. They left Pi Hahiroth and passed through the sea into the desert, and when they had traveled for three days in the Desert of Etham, they camped at Marah. They left Marah and went to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there. - Num 33:5-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the journey unfolds one camp at a time: Sukkoth, Etham, Pi Hahiroth, then through the sea, then Marah, then Elim. Each name marks a place where God's people stopped, rested, and were sustained. Two of these stand out. At Pi Hahiroth they "passed through the sea" — the great deliverance where God split the waters and drowned the pursuing army. And at Elim they found twelve springs and seventy palm trees, an oasis of refreshment after the desert.

The pattern of the wilderness journey is instructive: God led them through impossible waters and also to places of sweet rest. There were Red Seas of deliverance and Elims of refreshment. Both were gifts from His hand. The same God who parts seas also plants palm trees by springs.

Our lives follow a similar rhythm. There are seasons when God does the impossible, making a way where there seemed to be none. And there are seasons of quiet refreshment, when He leads us to still waters and lets us rest. We need both, and He provides both in their time.

Notice too that Marah, a place of bitter water, came before Elim's springs. Often the sweetest refreshment follows the hardest stretch. If you are in a bitter season now, take heart — God knows the way to Elim, and He is leading you there. He gives living water to all who come to Christ, a spring welling up to eternal life that never runs dry (John 4:14).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you seen God make a way through an "impossible sea" in your life?
2. Are you in a Marah season or an Elim season right now?
3. How does Christ, the living water, refresh you in dry times?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You lead me through impossible waters and to places of rest. In bitter seasons, help me trust that You know the way to refreshment, and satisfy me with the living water of Christ. Amen.
